scope: configuration resource counts, not per-device or per-rule runtime budgets
database: dedicated MySQL 8.4 through the Hyper-V test VM
verified: New quotas default to unlimited; older updates preserve omitted resource limits; explicit zero blocks growth.
Role and tenant isolation, numeric bounds, server-owned usage and observation timestamps.
Concurrent device binding and domain creation admit exactly one at a limit of one; denied bindings remain pending.
Concurrent rule creation on three distinct edges shares one account-wide rule or port allowance.
TCP and UDP using the same numeric port consume separate slots; HTTP sites consume a rule but no shared-listener port slot.
Lowered limits allow edits without growth; moving a port retains and charges the old reservation.
A deleted rule's orphan reservation remains charged until expiry; valid expiry restores capacity.
Repeated additive migration restores owners from current rules and creation audits, recreates the owner index and preserves saved limits.
Unattributed live legacy reservations block finite port growth until expiry or ownership repair.
Successful idempotent domain creation retries do not consume another slot.
